# Draft:Battle of Orlau

----
The Battle of Orlau (sometimes referred to as the Battle of Orlau–Frankenau) was a minor engagement on the Eastern Front during World War I, fought on 24 August 1914 near the villages of Orlau and Frankenau in East Prussia (modern-day northern Poland). The battle involved forces of the Russian Second Army attacking defensive positions held by the German Eighth Army. Although limited in scale, the engagement influenced troop movements prior to the Battle of Tannenberg later that month.
In August 1914, the Russian Empire launched an invasion of East Prussia as part of its opening operations of the war, aiming to relieve pressure on France by forcing Germany to divert forces from the Western Front. The German Eighth Army, though numerically inferior, relied on interior lines of communication, prepared positions, and effective use of terrain to slow the Russian advance.
As the Russian Second Army advanced westward, a series of skirmishes and minor engagements took place. The villages of Orlau and Frankenau lay along important local routes and became points of contact between advancing Russian units and German screening forces tasked with delaying the invasion.
On 24 August 1914, Russian forces attacked German positions near Orlau and Frankenau. German troops, occupying prepared defensive positions, resisted the attacks despite Russian numerical superiority. The fighting consisted primarily of small-unit infantry actions supported by artillery fire.
After several hours of combat, German forces conducted a planned withdrawal toward positions closer to Tannenberg. This delaying action slowed the Russian advance and allowed German commanders additional time to concentrate forces for the decisive battles that followed.
The Battle of Orlau did not result in a decisive tactical outcome, but it played a role in shaping the operational situation in East Prussia. The delay imposed on the Russian Second Army contributed to the German ability to regroup and later encircle Russian forces during the Battle of Tannenberg (26–30 August 1914), which ended in a major German victory.
Although not widely documented as a standalone engagement, the Battle of Orlau is representative of the numerous small actions that characterized the early stages of the East Prussian campaign. Such engagements influenced movement, timing, and coordination, demonstrating the importance of delaying actions in early World War I operations on the Eastern Front.
